title: Ancient Trees in the Philippines: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Strangler figs you can walk inside, a spring at the roots of an enchanted balete. {trees} trees across {places} places in the Philippines.
intro: You can walk inside the most famous fig on our Philippine map. At Balete Park in Maria Aurora the host tree has long gone, leaving a cage of fused roots around a hollow, billed as the largest balete in Asia, a claim we found no measurement for. A balete is a strangler fig, starting as a seed in another tree's branches. On Siquijor, the island the rest of the country links with folk healers, a spring rises at the roots of another one and feeds a pool of doctor fish. Their ages, 400 to about 600 years, are tradition rather than counted, and neither species is settled. The odd one out is a rain tree, locally called an acacia, in a church patio in Meycauayan, where Manuel L. Quezon is said to have played as a young sexton in 1890. If you know any of them better, tell us.
